question: Which of the following rivers originates in the Milam glacier in the Nepal Himalayas where it is known as Goriganga?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Saryu.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Goriganga**, also known as the **Sarda or Saryu river**, rises in the **Milam glacier of the Nepal Himalayas.**
 
• It is known as **Kali or Chauk** as it joins the **Ghaghara** along the **Indo-Nepal border.**
 
• Before emptying into the **Sharda River near Pancheshwar** at the **India–Nepal border**, it passes through the cities of **Kapkot, Bageshwar, and Seraghat.**
 
• In **Sitapur District, Uttar Pradesh**, the Sharda River merges with the **Ghaghara River.**
 
• In India, **Lower Ghaghara** is also referred to as** Sarayu**.
 
• Particularly as it passes through** Ayodhya,** the city where** Rama** was born.
 
• The ancient **Indian epic Ramayana** makes numerous mentions of the** saryu river.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Gomti:**

 
 
• The Gomti River, is an alluvial river of the Ganga Plain and originates **near Mainkot, from Gomat Taala lake also known as– 'Fulhar Jheel' in Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• It is one of the **Ganges' tributaries.**
 
• It is believed that **washing in the Gomti on Ekadashi **can **wash sins away** because the river is thought to be the **son of Rishi Vashishtha.**
 
 
 
• **Tons:**
 
 
• The Tons river originates from the **Ruinsara snout** and flows through Garhwal, the western part of the Himalayan state of Uttaranchal, edging Himachal Pradesh.
 
• It is a **Yamuna tributary** that **flows through Uttarakhand's Garhwal region** and **touches Himachal Pradesh.**
 
 
 
• **Karamnasa:**
 
 
• It is one of the **Ganges' tributaries.**
 
• The Karmanasa originates at a height of 350 meters (1,150 ft) on the northern face of the **Kaimur Range near Sarodag in the Kaimur district of Bihar.**
